outline: 643 Area of Composite Figures with Special Quadrilaterals

examples.solution_text:
The parallel sides are $4\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$. Substitute into the area formula.
$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\27&=\frac{h(4+8)}{2}\\27&=\frac{12h}{2}\end{aligned}$
Multiply both sides by $2$, then divide both sides by $12$.
$\begin{aligned}54&=12h\\4.5&=h\\h&=4.5\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
The height is the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides, even when those sides are drawn vertically.

The parallel sides are vertical, so the horizontal perpendicular distance is $h=4.4\text{ m}$.
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\33&=\frac{4.4(10+q)}{2}\end{aligned}$
Multiply both sides by $2$, then divide both sides by $4.4$.
$\begin{aligned}66&=4.4(10+q)\\15&=10+q\end{aligned}$
Subtract the known parallel side from the sum.
$\begin{aligned}q&=15-10\\q&=5\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

methods.description: Substitute the known area and parallel sides into the trapezium formula, multiply both sides by 2 and divide by the sum of the parallel sides. Identify the perpendicular distance regardless of orientation or context.

examples.derivation: 27=h(4+8)/2=12h/2. Multiplying by 2 gives 54=12h; dividing by 12 gives h=4.5 cm. Substitution gives 4.5(4+8)/2=27 cm². This adapts source question 7a using different values and preserves its inverse-operation method. The diagram marks parallel sides and a perpendicular height without revealing the answer.

33=4.4(10+q)/2. Multiplying by 2 gives 66=4.4(10+q); dividing by 4.4 gives 15=10+q; subtracting 10 gives q=5 m. Substitution gives 4.4(10+5)/2=33 m². Source questions 8c and 9b support finding an unknown parallel side. The diagram correctly shows vertical parallel sides and their horizontal perpendicular separation.
